name: Filter Coffee
steps: Set a clean South Indian coffee filter over its lower chamber. Add the coffee powder to the upper chamber and level it gently without packing it tightly.
Place the pressing disc if your filter uses one, pressing only lightly. Pour in the hot measured water carefully, cover and allow the decoction to drip into the lower chamber.
Let the filter drain naturally rather than stirring or forcing the grounds. Meanwhile, heat the milk in a saucepan until steaming, watching so it does not boil over.
Combine the decoction and hot milk, starting with a little less decoction if you prefer a milder cup. Stir in sugar to taste until dissolved.
For a little froth, carefully pour between two heat-safe vessels from a low height, or whisk briefly. Divide into cups and serve hot.
tips: Adjust the decoction-to-milk ratio to taste.
substitutions: Any substitution changes the recipe: recheck allergies, Jain rules and quantities.
notes: Prices are sample ingredient-cost assumptions. Replace with supplier rates before procurement.
